item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
A single section of submarine fiber optic cable is about 100 km between repeaters and masses about 140,000 kg. There are thousands of these. Fiber optics cables aren't either routers or computers. Neither are the buildings that house the big trunk hubs and similar hard brick and mortar infrastructure of the internet. Buildings are more massive than strawberries [citation needed].

A strawberry masses about 20 grams. The total mass of the electrons that at any given moment are flowing through internet infrastructure is about 50 g (so a big polyploid strawberry), but this doesn't include end use devices, which roughly triples this. This isn't actually relevant here, though, because this object doesn't have any dynamic electrical activity. It is just the data on the internet, not the actual packets and flow.

If you just count the increase in energy levels in storage media with Internet accessible data, then the total mass is only .6 micrograms.

I would interpret it thus: It is all the information accessible by enumerating:

 for every ip address for every port that responds to http for every http endpoint (url/method) that doesn't 404 for every combination of auth/cookies/etc store the info

That would pick up things with no in-links (unlike, say, a web spider), and basically anything accessible on the public internet. It wouldn't pick up:

  • Stuff hidden behind a vpn
  • Stuff not exposed via http (eg. ftp)
  • Anything on the TOR network (which is, I think, what Aridorn was referring to)

That initially bothered me too, but the phrasing seems to lend itself to indicating the agent writing it was a little "salt of the earth". If he's around middle-aged and not exactly the sort of person to be concerned with niceties (which makes perfect sense for an experienced agent), then he probably paid a modicum of attention to the news, heard "pills" and early suppositions of overdose, and that was it in his mind, as far as he's concerned Ledger was probably found dead in a position of still trying to cram more Damn Illegal Pills down his throat.

Whether it could actually be considered an overdose, or whether it would be proper/nicer/more considerate to refer to it as a "severe drug interaction" or something doesn't really matter, because it's in-character for the agent to just call him "that actor who overdosed".
